solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where art lover may be, catching the setter's hint

indicators.note: the gallery phrase catches, or traps, the setter's contraction inside it

parts.note: an art lover may well be found in the Tate gallery: IN TATE
the setter speaking of themself says I'M, a contraction of 'I am' read as the setter's

explanation.surface: A gallery-goer is spotted while overhearing the setter drop a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The TATE is the London art gallery; the contraction goes inside it, after IN and the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to suggest or imply something indirectly, which is to hint at it.

clue.text: Inspired current prince inspired by Kelly?

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: being inspired by something means breathing it in, so the prince is drawn inside the outlaw's name

parts.note: Ned Kelly was the Australian bushranger
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A current royal draws inspiration from the actress Grace Kelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelly suggests Grace Kelly, but it is the outlaw Ned Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired in its literal sense means breathed in, which is what inhaled means.

clue.text: Having raised temperature, swallow hot drink

indicators.note: in a down entry the letter for temperature is raised to the top, moving from the end to the front

parts.note: to eat is to swallow food

explanation.surface: A feverish patient is told to swallow a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised temperature' sounds like a fever, but it means the letter T is lifted to the top of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a beverage normally served steaming, made by infusing leaves in boiling water.

clue.text: Cook boils meat mass — this gives you energy

indicators.note: to cook something up is to alter it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A recipe: boil a lot of meat, and it will give you energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the body's set of chemical processes that turn food into usable fuel.

clue.text: Drained river? Bound to go across it

indicators.note: the bound word goes across the river letter, spanning it so the letter sits inside

parts.note: bound and tied both mean fastened with rope

explanation.surface: Is the river empty? A bridge is bound to span it.
explanation.walkthrough: The river letter goes after TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling tired is feeling drained, with energy exhausted.

clue.text: Strengthen lead in tennis, having an advantage

indicators.note: the lead, or front letter, of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: only its first letter is used
to be one up is to be ahead of a rival

explanation.surface: A tennis player at advantage needs to strengthen the lead to win the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' and 'advantage' sound like tennis scoring, but lead picks the first letter and the advantage is the phrase ONE UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone up muscles is to firm and strengthen them through exercise.

clue.text: Players' line from the start of Ode to a Revolutionary?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Actors read a line from a poem dedicated to a famous revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The players are darts players, not actors: the oche is the line they stand behind to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the oche is the marked line on the floor behind which a thrower must stand.

clue.text: Offering instruction that is about banking old money and high loan

indicators.note: the reversed letters bank, or hold, the coin as a bank keeps money
the two letters turn about, so they read backwards

parts.note: IE is short for id est, that is
the ducat was an old gold coin

indicators.note: being high is being intoxicated, so the letters of loan are muddled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An instructive account of banks, old coinage and a large loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' and 'old money' sound financial, but banking is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Educational describes something that informs or teaches, giving instruction.

clue.text: Cover payment of leader with a different kind of hesitation

indicators.note: with a different hesitation means the hesitation in the leader word is swapped for another

parts.note: a premier is a head of government
UM is a hesitation sound like ER, which it replaces

explanation.surface: A leader hesitates differently before agreeing to the cover payment.
explanation.walkthrough: PREMIER ends in ER, itself a hesitation; swapping in the other one gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance premium is the regular sum paid to keep a policy giving cover.

clue.text: Denied profit, succeeded getting subsidies

parts.note: gain and profit both mean benefit
aid means financial support such as subsidies

explanation.surface: A firm was refused profit, having managed to get grants.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so gainsaid means denied.

clue.text: Play rock 'n' roll hit, deprived of telephone use

indicators.note: the hit title loses those letters, as if they were taken away from it

parts.note: Heartbreak Hotel was Elvis Presley's 1956 hit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put on a rock 'n' roll record but not to use the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the last three letters of the Elvis title leaves HEARTBREAK HO, then USE completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak House is a 1919 drama by George Bernard Shaw, so it is an example of a stage work.

clue.text: Going straight home to wear wig, a bald drunk

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wear the home word, holding it inside them as clothing holds a body
drunk letters are scrambled, so wig a bald are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
IN means at home

explanation.surface: A bald drunk heads home to put on his wig.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters for home sit after LAWAB in the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A former criminal who is going straight has become an honest citizen who obeys the law.

clue.text: Partners smuggling crack before arrest for kind of crime

indicators.note: the partners smuggle the blow in between them

parts.note: in bridge West and East are partners, W and E
a crack can be a sharp blow, a hit
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A criminal couple are smuggling crack cocaine before being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack reads as the drug, but here it means a sharp blow.
explanation.definitionFit: White-collar crime is fraud or embezzlement committed by office professionals.

clue.text: Saving Italy's capital, or one of its capitals

parts.note: saving and bar both mean except

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word is taken

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A question about rescuing Rome, Italy's capital, or one of its other capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Bari is the capital of Apulia, a region of Italy, so 'its capitals' means Italy's regional capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari, on the Adriatic coast, is the regional capital city of Apulia in southern Italy.

clue.text: You no longer must accept hard time: it's all over

indicators.note: the old pronoun must accept, or take in, the hard word

parts.note: thou is the archaic form of you, no longer used
rough can mean hard or harsh

explanation.surface: Someone doing a tough prison stretch is told: accept it, it's over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's all over' sounds like the end, but the definition means everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means in every part of something, so all over it.

clue.text: Did some boring training with my boss

parts.note: drill is training through repeated exercises
the setter's boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: A worker complains of tedious training sessions run alongside their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but here it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drilled is the past tense of drill, to bore a hole with a rotating tool.

clue.text: Break down copper with small crack

parts.note: a copper is a police officer, here a DI or detective inspector
to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: Metal breaks down when it has a little crack.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests the metal Cu, but it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve is to disintegrate or decompose into parts.

clue.text: Articles by the writer writing to overturn conviction

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: in this across clue overturning turns the manuscript letters back to front

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An author pens articles intended to overturn a criminal conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' looks legal in the surface but here means a firmly held belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is a firmly held belief that there is no god, so it is a conviction in that sense.

clue.text: Fool is maintaining record's purity

indicators.note: the fool word maintains, or holds, the record within it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
EP is an extended-play record
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool insists that a recording keeps its purity.
explanation.walkthrough: The record goes inside ASS after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the absence of harmful bacteria, a sterile cleanliness or freedom from contamination.

clue.text: Comic figure, a big hit entertaining the disheartened Republican

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the hit word entertains, or houses, the other letters inside it

parts.note: in cricket a six is a big hit clean over the boundary

indicators.note: the heart, or middle letter, is removed, leaving the two ends

parts.note: only its outer letters are used

explanation.surface: A cartoon hero, a smash success, plays host to a gloomy Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Asterix the Gaul is the hero of the French comic-book series by Goscinny and Uderzo.

clue.text: Had to follow medic getting overwhelmed

indicators.note: the possession word follows the doctor, so it comes second

parts.note: had and owned both mean possessed

explanation.surface: Someone had to wait behind the doctor and was swamped by it all.
explanation.walkthrough: DR is the doctor's title abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowned can mean swamped or submerged, as a sound is drowned out by a louder one.

clue.text: Respected female finished suppressing desire

indicators.note: the finished word suppresses, or holds down within it, the desire

parts.note: done means finished
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: An esteemed woman has finally managed to suppress her longings.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most senior and esteemed woman in a field.

clue.text: The city of Paris?

definitions.meaning: the surface asks for a city, as if naming the French capital itself
in fact Paris is the Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen caused the Trojan War, so his city is meant

explanation.surface: A quiz question apparently asking for the name of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Paris is a person here: the prince of Greek legend, son of King Priam.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy was the home of Paris, son of King Priam, in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Crook and prison pal showing how partners may be joined

definitions.text: showing how partners may be joined

parts.note: a con is a convict, a crook
jug is slang for prison
an ally is a friend or pal

explanation.surface: A criminal and his cellmate become so close it looks like a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjugally means in the manner of marriage, describing how husband and wife are united.

clue.text: WWII belligerent to criticise Munich Agreement at first

indicators.note: the German agreement comes at first, ahead of the criticism

parts.note: ja is German for yes, an agreement heard in Munich
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A wartime nation denounces the 1938 Munich Agreement from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The Munich Agreement was the 1938 pact with Hitler, but here it is simply a German yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan fought on the Axis side in the Second World War from 1941.

clue.text: Broadcast set to receive unknown viewer's complaint

indicators.note: the scrambled letters receive the unknown inside them
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A television set picks up an unknown broadcast, prompting complaints from viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: Viewer suggests a TV audience, but it means an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an ailment of the eye.

clue.text: Perhaps who e.g. mum favouring old sister hugs

parts.note: a mother is an example of a relative
pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the nun hugs, or encloses, the letter for old

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: Mum prefers the older sister, who gets all the hugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' and 'e.g.' both flag that who is one example of the grammatical term wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Who, which and that are pronouns introducing a relative clause, so grammarians class them as such.

clue.text: American friend has gone round the globe

indicators.note: going round turns the friend word, so it reads upward in this down entry

parts.note: bro is American slang for a friend

explanation.surface: An American pal has travelled around the world.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere, the shape of a globe.

clue.text: Spurning love, copies ancient king

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the love letter is thrown out of the copies word

parts.note: to xerox something is to photocopy it
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A monarch of old rejects romance and imitates others instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes the Great was a Persian ruler who invaded Greece in 480 BC.

clue.text: Rocky's incompetent boxing extremely suspect

indicators.note: the incompetent word boxes in, or encloses, the extreme letters

parts.note: unable means not competent to do something

indicators.note: the extreme, outermost letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Rocky Balboa, the film boxer, is called hopeless in the ring and suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocky the boxing film hero pulls towards a name, but it means shaky or wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocky is unsteady and liable to wobble or collapse.
